components.name: Framed Screen
components.description: A whole app capture in a 12px dark frame under a window strip; opens full size on click.

narrative.overview:
The site is a dark, quiet room with the lights on the work. The ground is a near-black blue (#0b0f14); everything the visitor reads sits on it in one typeface, Geist, at one weight family; the brightest things on any page are the real app screens, white captures held in dark rounded frames. Colour is almost absent: one orange for the one action that matters in the view, and three soft tints that say whether a product is live, opening soon or coming. Depth comes from borders and tone steps, not from shadows or glows.

The system is borrowed in spirit from the premium product sites the owner pointed at (Notion, Linear, the Google Store) and kept plain for a trade audience: short sentences, prices stated up front, nothing that moves unless it is arriving. The site is **dark only**. There is no light theme and no theme switch; the logo is always the reversed one.

Above 1440px the page does not stretch a phone layout: the root font-size grows (16px at 1440, about 18px at 1920, 20px at 2560), every component is sized in rem, and the content column grows with the screen, so a big monitor sees the same page in the same proportions, larger.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface (Geist 400/500/600/700), headlines at 600 with tight tracking (-0.02em), no uppercase labels.
One ground, two surface steps (#131922, #1a2230), hairline borders at 10% white.
One orange (#f25c1f) per view, on the primary action only; hover turns secondary controls and links orange.
Real product screens, whole, never cropped, never upscaled past their own pixels, framed at a 12px radius.
One band per page: the surface tone held by a hairline above and below.
A once-only 12px fade-up as sections arrive; nothing moves with reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: One orange button per view. While a page's own orange action is on screen, the nav's Book a demo steps back to the secondary style (board.js adds `.nav.quiet`); it returns when none is in view.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: No gradients, glows, blur halos or coloured shadows anywhere. Borders and tone steps carry depth.

rules.name: The No Caps Rule
rules.body: No tracked uppercase labels anywhere; labels are sentence case at weight 500.

rules.name: The Ruler Figures Rule
rules.body: Money, hours and counts use tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) so columns line up.

rules.name: The Borders Do The Work Rule
rules.body: Depth is a tone step plus a 1px hairline. A hover lifts a card 2px and firms its edge to the control edge; it never adds a shadow.

dos: Do keep the site dark only: #0b0f14 ground, the reversed logo, `theme-color` #0b0f14.
Do put exactly one orange button in any view, and let hover turn secondary controls and links orange.
Do show the real app's screens whole, from the harness with synthetic data, each with its `.json` provenance sidecar; the example business is Southline Formwork Pty Ltd and no other.
Do size components in rem so the page grows with the root font-size above 1440.
Do state prices with their source and GST basis (inc GST), and highlight at most one money fact per paragraph.
Do keep text at 14px or more at phone width and secondary text at 4.5:1 or better.
donts: Don't add a light theme, a theme switch or a second stylesheet; tokens live on `:root` in board.css.
Don't crop a screen, upscale it past its own pixels, or put a glow, gradient or blur halo behind it.
Don't add testimonials, customer logos, client names, invented figures or photos of real crews or sites.
Don't name a competitor in a comparison table or in public copy outside the dated /compare pages: it is "other apps".
Don't use uppercase tracked labels, a second typeface or a colour outside the tokens above.
Don't load a script, font or API from a host the CSP in `public/_headers` does not list (self-hosted scripts, Google Fonts only).
